title: Conversational brain model A/B through the real obey-voice brain seam

config_layering.note: config brain_provider is grok, but every persona profile pins provider ollama, so the persona overlay decides. The ollama path is what the live session logs show, and it is what is measured here.

system_prompt.elements: persona + environment + skills catalog + turn instruction (brain.AssembleSystemPrompt, ollama policy)

gate.g5: G1-G4 must hold in both history conditions
gate.p95_caveat: nearest-rank on n=15; read as worst observed, not a distributional claim

prompts.text: In one sentence, tell me what you're good at.
Explain briefly what a vector database is.
I've got two hours before a meeting and three tasks: prep slides, review a pull request, and reply to email. How should I order them, and why?
Should I use a local model or a cloud model for voice? Keep it short.

filled_history.source: scripts/brain_bench/history.go — real dialogue about this repository's work, tail-trimmed to fit

notes: Latency only. Nothing here judges response quality; that is the user's judgment in real use.
Each sample resets history to the condition baseline first, so prompt size is constant across reps.
route_ms is the synchronous skill-router embedding call and is included in ttft_ms, because the user waits for it.

ttft_ms stops on the first streamed token; speak_ttft_ms stops on the first segment that survives pipeline.SpeechProjection — the product's own path from a model segment to TTS (think filter, voice gate, CleanForVoice, speakability, repeat suppression), shared code rather than a copy. On a reasoning model the gap between the two is the reasoning prologue, which nobody hears.
~/.obey was read, never written. No model was pulled or deleted. Models were unloaded (not removed) to measure cold load.
